players.product: Falcon platform AI: Charlotte AI detection triage and SafeMind agentic security, run on rented AI compute (Cerebras inference, CoreWeave GPUs, NVIDIA NIM)

quarterly_data.signal: President Michael Sentonas and CFO Burt Podbere, long-term targets pulled in: CrowdStrike now believes it can reach $10 billion ending ARR within FY 2030 (previously by the end of FY 2031) and $20 billion within FY 2035 (previously by the end of FY 2036); the $5.8 billion Q2 ending ARR is about 30% of the way to $20 billion. CFO's first view of FY 2028: 20% plus year-over-year net new ARR growth, net new ARR equal to or greater than $1,626 million (after the FY 2027 midpoint of $1,355 million), and a 32.5% plus free cash flow margin (FY 2027: 30% plus) even with capex rising to 11%-12% next year; the FY 2029 target model is unchanged (subscription gross margin 82%-85%, operating margin 28%-32%, free cash flow margin 34%-38%) against 81% subscription gross margin and 24% operating margin in the first half of FY 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: $10 billion ARR within FY 2030; $20 billion ARR within FY 2035; FY 2028 net new ARR equal to or greater than $1,626 million; FY 2028 free cash flow margin 32.5% plus

quarterly_data.signal: President Michael Sentonas and CFO Burt Podbere, market sizing (company estimates): CrowdStrike's addressable market reaches $565 billion by calendar year 2034; the total AI security opportunity $215 billion by calendar 2034 (agentic security $115 billion, agentic SOC $52 billion, agentic identity $48 billion), and capturing 3.5% of it would add $7.5 billion of ARR, roughly 38% of the $20 billion target; CrowdStrike has averaged roughly 4% share of the security market it addresses over the last six years and has around 20% of modern endpoint; reaching $1.8 billion agentic SOC ARR needs a 13% CAGR from Next-Gen SIEM and $1.7 billion agentic identity ARR a 14% CAGR; CY 2034 international market opportunity $244 billion (CFO goal: a 50/50 U.S. / international mix, with more spending on international sales and sovereign cloud); white space in the existing customer base $29 billion at 2Q FY2027, up from $21 billion a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: $565 billion addressable market by 2034; AI security opportunity $215 billion; $7.5 billion potential AI security ARR at 3.5% share; $29 billion white space

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz and Chief AI and Autonomous Systems Officer Bartley Richardson on SafeMind: in CrowdStrike's benchmarks Blue Solano had 37% better detection rates than Frontier Lab One and 29% better than Frontier Lab Two, Red Tempest cost 66% or 78% less per task, the blue side was up to 99% more cost effective and detection 6 times faster; Richardson: a 70% increase in accuracy versus an off-the-shelf model and harness and a 99% cost reduction, from $10 to $0.03 per remediation. Monetization (Kurtz): CrowdStrike tokens sold in initial token packs and token expansion packs through Falcon Flex, 'a different monetization stream'; SafeMind can be consumed only by Falcon Flex customers; direct model access goes through the QuiltWorks partner program, in preview and rolling out over the back half of the year; a model routing layer makes CrowdStrike 'a distribution path for the Frontier Labs' ('we want to get paid through the whole token flow process'). Kurtz: CrowdStrike generates 7 trillion security events per day and has 270 PhDs, 300 AI researchers and 500 threat researchers, with R&D investment over $1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 37% better detection; 6 times faster detection; 99% cost reduction ($10 to $0.03 per remediation)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurtz: AI DR saw a 79x increase in uptake just after 3 months (EDR saw 10x 3 quarters from launch); AI DR is the category and Falcon Guardian the product, the earlier AI DR product 'is going to be retired' and 'Pricing will go up on Guardian'; Guardian covers agents on endpoints, in cloud workloads / containers and SaaS agents, built on the Pangea acquisition plus the Falcon sensor and platform; Amazon was its biggest design partner. President Michael Sentonas: Guardian became generally available to every customer during the keynote and is a licensed entitlement turned on through Falcon Flex; the Agentic Identity Provider builds on the SGNL acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: 79x increase in AI DR uptake after 3 months

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Burt Podbere, Falcon Flex and partners: the average ending ARR uplift from a non-Flex to a Flex deal rose to 40% from 34% last year; Flex logos are now 50/50 enterprise / non-enterprise versus 61% / 39% at 2Q26 under a Flex-first sales motion, and he envisions a time with no non-Flex deals; 100,000 organizations as customers as of Q1 and 34 modules; eight partners each have lifetime TCV of $1 billion, 19 each $500 million and 65 each $100 million, and 890 partners doubled their business with CrowdStrike year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: Flex ARR uplift 40% vs 34%; eight partners with $1 billion lifetime TCV; 890 partners doubled their business

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Burt Podbere on costs: prices of storage have gone up and CrowdStrike has worked with its strategic vendors to lock in certain pricing; gross margin levers are running more compute and storage in cheaper public-cloud regions (Amazon West 2 versus West 1), volume discounts with its public cloud providers, migrating the more expensive workloads to its private cloud and using AI to consolidate data stores; CrowdStrike put $1 billion into R&D last year.

Chief Business Officer Daniel Bernard on Anthropic: CrowdStrike products went live on the Anthropic marketplace (announced that day; Anthropic's Ash ElDifrawi: CrowdStrike is the first security partner there), so customers can apply their Anthropic commit to CrowdStrike purchases; the two companies are building Anthropic-powered modules in the Falcon platform that a customer can activate with its own Anthropic API key, 'with us being involved in the token flow'; CrowdStrike was an inaugural founding member of Project Glasswing. CEO George Kurtz: CrowdStrike partners with Anthropic, OpenAI and others because customers want their data to stay with a trusted security partner while using different models.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: partner (marketplace channel and planned model supplier)
